name: Felix Carrera-Wei
description:
Felix Carrera-Wei is the operator Kyle would have been if Kyle had said yes to a particular contract eleven years ago instead of saying no. The contract has not been named in canon. Felix has, on three occasions in the past four years, suggested that Kyle might want to know what the contract was. Kyle has not asked. Felix has not pressed. The not-asking and the not-pressing are the entire shape of their relationship, which is professional, hostile, and oddly intimate in the way that a long-running dispute can be intimate when neither party has the appetite to escalate.

Felix operates at Kyle's tier or above. Heavy implant load, all of it visible (the visible chrome is the statement; Felix wants you to read the catalog before you read the man). Specializes in contracts the freelance market has flagged as morally untenable — slaver extractions, child-organ-network recovery, corponation black-bag work that ends in bodies. Felix takes them because Felix has read the work and decided the work is the work, and the alternative is some other operator does it less well. He is not, in his own framing, a villain. He is a careful man working at a level of moral ambiguity most operators do not have the discipline for.

Kyle does not agree with Felix's framing. Kyle has also not yet refused a contract Felix routed to him, which Kyle is aware of in the way you are aware of a debt you have not yet acknowledged.
heritage: Spanish-Hokkien. Father's family from Barcelona via the Mediterranean climate-collapse waves of the 2120s. Mother's family from Xiamen via the Taiwan diaspora resettlement programs of the 2160s. Felix speaks four languages well and has stopped advertising which ones.
specialty: high-risk contract execution; contracts the freelance market refuses on principle; corponation black-bag wetwork; recovery operations that other operators decline
method: prepares for weeks before any contract. Brings the maximum sustainable hardware load. Closes contracts cleanly and disappears. Has, by Echo's count, never been on the same continent twice in any single year.
code: the contract is the contract; the moral calculus belongs to whoever wrote the contract, not to the operator who executes it; the operator's only ethical obligation is to execute cleanly. This is, in his framing, the most honest position a freelancer can hold. It is also the position Kyle has spent his life rejecting in himself.
signature_gear: a custom Korova Arms KA-12 'Ghost Note' subharmonic rifle (Tier 5, the kind of weapon that costs more than most apartments); full chrome augmentation, visible at the temples and forearms, manufacturer markings deliberately exposed; a watch that is older than any of his hardware and which he does not explain; a passport that reads as Tier 5 in any jurisdictional database Felix is willing to be read in
relationship_to_kyle: recurring rival, occasional reluctant collaborator. They have met four times. Three times on opposite sides of the same contract. Once, in 2222, in a hotel lobby in the GLMZ Tier 5 corridor where Felix bought Kyle a drink and Kyle did not finish it. Felix views Kyle as the operator Kyle could be if Kyle accepted what Felix has accepted. Kyle views Felix as the operator Kyle could be if Kyle accepted what Kyle has spent his life refusing.
aesthetic: impeccable. Three-piece suits when meetings call for them. Tactical clothing when work calls for it. Always groomed. Always polite. The kind of man you would not pick out of a crowd unless you already knew what to look for.
spin_off_hook: Felix takes a contract Kyle refuses. The contract goes wrong in a specific way that makes Felix call Kyle in the middle of it — not for help, but to explain. The conversation is the story. Kyle does not arrive in time to alter the outcome. Felix walks away alive and richer, and the body the contract was about is in a Vultures van, and Kyle has to decide whether the conversation Felix initiated was a confession, a recruitment, or a goodbye.
